title: The daemon composes turns with no law when the constitution is missing
body:
## Summary
`wiring.build` loads the constitution with `load_or_empty`, so a deployment whose law is missing runs every turn under "(no law on file)" instead of refusing to start, while the module and the doctor both say a turn with no law should not start.

## Description
`src/athena/core/constitution.py:76-79` says Athena runs without law "only on purpose, never by accident" and `:247-249` says `load_or_empty` is for the doctor and fixtures and that "a turn with no law is a turn that should not have started". `src/athena/cli.py:150` makes the doctor's constitution stage a `fail` for the same reason. But `src/athena/wiring.py:280` (`constitution = load_or_empty(constitution_dir)`) is the production build of the daemon, so the turn frame composes `Constitution.block('law')` as `(no law on file)` (`src/athena/core/constitution.py:191`) and the run proceeds. Fixed: wiring calls `load()` and lets `ConstitutionMissing` stop the build (or the daemon refuses `/run` with a named reason while `/health` says why), and only the doctor and fixtures keep `load_or_empty`. Technique: prompt-assembly/layered-composition (the law layer is owned and mandatory); the repo's own rule in core/constitution.py.

## Flow
- set ATHENA_CONSTITUTION to an empty directory (or ship a wheel without athena/constitution/)
- start the daemon -> wiring.build -> load_or_empty returns Constitution(sections={})
- POST /run -> the system prompt's first block is "(no law on file)" and the turn runs
- fix, in build order: test in tests/test_wiring.py that build() with an empty constitution dir raises ConstitutionMissing (seed red), then switch wiring.py:280 to load(), then re-run tests/daemon and tests/e2e for fixtures that relied on the empty fallback

## Expected impact
An operator whose build lost its law finds out at boot instead of after a lawless turn; nothing changes for an installation that carries law.md. Could break: a test fixture that builds a daemon from a tmp root with no constitution and no checkout marker.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a missing law stops the daemon instead of running lawless turns
Before: wiring.py:280 uses load_or_empty; build() with an empty constitution dir returns a daemon whose law block is "(no law on file)" (read from the code path; constitution.py:262-268)
After: build() raises ConstitutionMissing naming every candidate it looked in
Method: simulation - walked the code path; the file is outside this round's write set (wiring.py belongs to another context and had another session's uncommitted edits)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/athena/wiring.py:280: constitution = load_or_empty(constitution_dir)
src/athena/core/constitution.py:247-249: "For the doctor and for fixtures ... The composer does not use this. A turn with no law is a turn that should not have started."
src/athena/cli.py:150-158: doctor stage is `fail` on ConstitutionMissing
src/athena/core/constitution.py:191: body = self.section(name) or f"(no {name} on file)"
instrument: tests/test_wiring.py: build() with ATHENA_CONSTITUTION pointing at an empty tmp dir must raise ConstitutionMissing; red today, green after wiring.py:280 calls load()

title: Nested object params are not validated: their properties and required are ignored
body:
## Summary
The gate's validator checks a param's own type, enum and bounds, but a param of type `object` whose schema declares nested `properties`, `required` or `additionalProperties: false` is accepted whatever it holds, so a page's or connector's declared nested constraints are never enforced at the gate.

## Description
`src/athena/core/validators.py:_check_value` recurses only through `items` (arrays); for a dict value it checks `type` and stops. `contracts.manifest.params_schema_problems` (`src/athena/contracts/manifest.py:51-88`) inspects only the top-level `properties`, so a manifest may declare `{"filter": {"type": "object", "properties": {"status": {"enum": ["open"]}}, "required": ["status"], "additionalProperties": false}}` and the gate admits `{"filter": {"anything": 1}}` to an AUTO call or onto a card. The module docstring names the subset (no nested object keywords), so this is a fail-open on a schema the door accepts without saying it will not enforce it. Technique: mcp-tools/tool-schema-design ("the published schema and the enforced schema must be the same artifact"). Fixed is one of two arms: (A) recurse `_check_value` into an object's `properties`/`required`/`additionalProperties` (a small growth of the subset, stdlib only), or (B) fail closed: a nested object schema carrying keywords the gate does not enforce refuses every call as malformed, the way an unknown type now does (63d1dac).

## Flow
- a page manifest declares an AUTO tool whose param `filter` is an object with nested `required` and an enum
- the model proposes the tool with `filter: {"x": {"deep": [1,2,3]}}`
- Catalog.validate -> check_schema -> _check_value(filter) checks type object only -> accept -> the call fires
- build order: tests in tests/core/test_validators.py for both arms (nested required missing, nested enum miss, nested extra key under additionalProperties false), seed red, implement the chosen arm, run tests/core tests/lane tests/harness

## Expected impact
Pages and connectors get the nested constraints they declared enforced before a card or an AUTO call; no in-tree manifest or connector spec declares a nested object schema today (checked builtin gmail.json and notion.json), so nothing in-tree changes. Could break: a third-party page whose nested schema is stricter than the calls it actually expects.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the gate enforces (or refuses) what a nested object schema declares
Before: a nested required/enum/additionalProperties constraint is enforced in 0 of 3 walked cases (validators.py has no dict recursion)
After: 3 of 3 refused under either arm
Method: simulation - three cases walked on the code; the build is a choice between growing the documented subset (ADR 0002) and failing closed, so it needs both arms measured against in-tree manifests
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/athena/core/validators.py (_check_value): recursion only under `if isinstance(value, list)` -> items; no branch for dict values
src/athena/contracts/manifest.py:63-84: params_schema_problems walks top-level properties only
src/athena/core/validators.py:3-7: the subset named in the docstring has no nested object keywords
instrument: tests/core/test_validators.py: three nested-object cases (missing nested required, nested enum miss, nested extra key under additionalProperties false); red today on both arms, then each arm measured for in-tree manifest regressions (0 expected)

title: An approved, unspent grant never lapses at the gate; only the lane checks expiry
body:
## Summary
`Approvals.consume` spends an approved row however long ago its card expired, so a replay that reaches the gate with an approval id days later still runs; the only expiry check on an approved row is `BrowserLane._reopened`, for a re-answer.

## Description
`src/athena/core/approvals.py:494-510`: `consume` is `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'approved' AND consumed_at IS NULL`, with no `expires_at` term, and `expire_due` (`:476-492`) only moves `pending` rows. `src/athena/harness/hooks.py:283-318` (`_check_grant`) checks status, match and spend, not age. `src/athena/lane/browser_lane.py:493-497` refuses a lapsed approved row only when the user answers it again. ADR 0038's own reasoning puts single use in the gate because "it does not depend on the route being the only caller that holds an approval id" (approvals.py:30-32); expiry of a grant has no such home. `DEFAULT_TTL`'s comment (approvals.py:81-83) promises "last week's proposal is never executed against this week's page". The decision the owner must make: does `expires_at` bound the grant (refuse a replay after it) or only the answer (a yes given in time is good until spent)? The first is a one-term change to `consume` plus a reason; the second wants the TTL comment corrected. Technique: hitl-approval/resume-after-decision ("re-validates the world before acting ... the grant or credential is still live").

## Flow
- a card is approved; the replay is refused before consume (the app was switched off, ADR 0060), leaving the row approved and unspent
- a week later any caller of PolicyHook.run_tool(..., approval_id=...) replays it
- _check_grant -> describe (approved) -> matches -> consume (no expiry term) -> the action runs
- fix, if the owner says the TTL bounds the grant: add `AND expires_at > ?` to consume, return a distinct `expired` refusal from _check_grant, test in tests/core/test_approvals.py and tests/harness

## Expected impact
Closes a week-old grant running against a page that has moved on, for any replay path, not only the lane's. Could break: an approval answered seconds before its expiry whose replay lands after it; that is the semantic question for the owner.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a grant cannot be spent after the life the card promised
Before: consume() spends an approved row with expires_at in the past (read: no expires_at term in the UPDATE)
After: consume() refuses it and the gate names `expired`
Method: simulation - the code path is plain, but which reading of expires_at is right is an owner call, so no arm was built
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/athena/core/approvals.py:504-510: UPDATE companion_approval SET consumed_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND status = 'approved' AND consumed_at IS NULL
src/athena/core/approvals.py:81-83: "short enough that last week's proposal is never executed against this week's page"
src/athena/lane/browser_lane.py:493-497: the only lapse check on an approved row, for a re-answer

title: A grant a racing decline just closed is refused as "already been spent"
body:
## Summary
When `decline_approved` closes an approved, unspent row between the gate's `describe` and its `consume`, the gate refuses with `approval_spent` and "has already been spent", which names a cause that did not happen.

## Description
`src/athena/harness/hooks.py:286-316`: `_check_grant` reads the grant (approved), then calls `approvals.consume`; `consume` returns `False` for any row that is not approved-and-unspent (`src/athena/core/approvals.py:494-510`), and the gate maps every `False` to `approval_spent` with the sentence "has already been spent on <tool>". A `decline_approved` (ADR 0060, `approvals.py:512-536`) landing between the two leaves the row `declined` and unspent, so the user who said no is told the action ran. Fixed: on `False`, re-read the row and name `user_denied` when it is declined, `approval_spent` only when `consumed_at` is set. Out of this round's write set (harness/hooks.py).

## Flow
- an approved row whose first replay was refused stays approved and unspent
- surface A answers approve again (replay starts, describe -> approved) while surface B answers decline -> decline_approved closes the row
- A's consume -> False -> Cancel(approval_spent, "has already been spent")
- fix order: a race test in tests/harness with the approvals table's describe pinned stale (as in tests/core/test_approvals.py's race test), seed red, then re-read on False in hooks.py

## Expected impact
The refusal says the user declined instead of claiming the action already ran; no behaviour change. Could break: a test pinning the approval_spent detail for a non-spent row.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refusal names the real cause
Before: 1 of 1 walked race says "already been spent" for a row with consumed_at NULL
After: the same race names user_denied
Method: simulation - walked; hooks.py is outside this round's write set
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/harness/hooks.py:310-315: if not self.approvals.consume(approval_id): return Cancel("approval_spent", f"approval {approval_id} has already been spent on {entry.name}", ...)
src/athena/core/approvals.py:529-536: decline_approved sets status 'declined' WHERE status = 'approved' AND consumed_at IS NULL
instrument: tests/harness: PolicyHook.run_tool with approval_id where describe returns the approved row and the table row was declined in between; assert reason user_denied (red today: approval_spent)
